Waterloo Regional Police Services - 2024 Budget Presentation
notes:
Ian McLean, Vice-Chair of the Waterloo Regional Police Services Board, presented key insights on the Waterloo Regional Police Services (WRPS) 2024 budget. The presentation encompassed an overview of the WRPS mandate, legislative requirements, the Police Services Act, the formulation process of the 2024 budget, findings from the strategic business plan community survey, WRPS staffing levels, historical officer expansion, and the proposed hiring strategy for the Police Services Board (PSB).

Police Chief Mark Crowell continued the presentation, addressing Regional support services, calls for service, total crime severity index, violent crime severity index, 2023 violent crime trends, 2023 major crimes, 2023 complex crime trends, growth of hate crimes in the Region, 2023 traffic safety trends, emergency response and public safety, investing in frontline technologies, alignment with community safety and wellbeing plan, community outreach and engagement, alternate mental health services, intimate partner violence, youth engagement strategy, 2024 budget drivers, annual cost for police services per resident, WRPS use of overtime, 2024 approved capital estimates, 2024 approved operating estimates, and budget investment areas.

In response to a question from the Committee, Chief Crowell indicated that, according to the latest report, the WRPS is on par and leading in the move towards total civilianization when compared to Ontario's Big 12 municipalities. More information will be provided to the Committee. 

In response to a question from the Committee, Chief Crowell stated that about 25% of the crime within the Region originates from outside the region, with factors such as highway access and shopping centers contributing to this dynamic. The WRPS is actively collaborating through integrated partnerships to address these challenges, and the police force is responding to and addressing these incidents to the best of their ability.

In response to a question, the Chief Crowell mentioned that WRPS is responding to schools more frequently than ever. The police force has maintained ongoing collaboration with education partners to establish the best possible protocols. Recognizing a growing concern across the spectrum, WRPS acknowledges and addresses the continuing issue of youth-related violence.

In response to a question from the Committee, Chief Crowell addressed the imperative need highlighted by municipal leaders for increased visibility and presence in communities. Despite the challenges of planning, WRPS is committed to maintaining a visible presence in downtown, uptown, and townships, responding to the ongoing request from the community. This budget reflects a commitment to frontline availability as a top priority, ensuring a variety of response modes such as on bike and foot patrols. Additionally, it emphasizes the importance of dedicating resources to build meaningful relationships with business owners, residents, and communities.

In response to a question from the Committee, Chief Crowell addressed concerns about the ability to increase the number of officers. He explained the success in onboarding new officers, with an average of approximately 48.6 officers per year, and highlighted the budgeted $2 million for this purpose. While minimum requirements are currently met through overtime, he emphasized the need to hire more officers for the well-being of the force, given the costliness of overtime. The overarching goal is to maintain a lean, efficient, and versatile approach to service delivery. Vice Chair McLean added that the issue of overtime is tied to the necessity for officers, stressing the importance of recruiting to ensure there is sufficient staff to effectively serve the community.

In response to a question from the committee, Chief Crowell addressed the demographics of the force. He emphasized that, in compliance with federal and provincial provisions, they are obligated to report on this aspect. Chief Crowell also discussed the demographics of the leadership structure within the team.

In response to a question from the Committee, Chief Crowell provided insights into the reserve and reserve funds, assuring the Committee that more detailed information would be shared. He emphasized that WRPS makes collaborative efforts to manage all finances with the utmost accountability, acting in full transparency to the Police Services Board and the community, and in accordance with the Board’s Reserve and Reserve Fund Management Policy.

items.title: 2024 Plan and Budget Presentation
notes:
Craig Dyer, Commissioner, Corporate Services, and Chief Financial Officer, presented the 2024 Plan and Budget. The presentation covered the current status of the 2024 operating budget, the proposed use of tax stabilization reserve in the preliminary 2024 budget, and the Regional funding for services that should be funded by Provincial revenues.

Continuing the presentation, Peter Sweeney, Commissioner, Community Services, brought attention to National Housing Day. He addressed the concerning growth of chronic homelessness in Waterloo Region, emphasizing the need to bridge the gap. P. Sweeney outlined four pillars crucial to closing this gap, which include responding to the current reality, transitioning to the future, creating a sustainable and equitable future, and maintaining existing solutions.

In response to inquiries from the Committee, P. Sweeney addressed the multifaceted challenges associated with closing the gap on chronic homelessness, emphasizing that the response needs to be equally comprehensive. He underscored the urgency of addressing immediate needs, cautioning that without intervention, the gap would only widen. P. Sweeney provided additional details on transitional housing, permanent housing, the necessity for a women's shelter, hybrid shelters, and the Lived Expertise Prototyping Project.

items.title: COR-CFN-23-040, Industrial Land Readiness - Interim Funding Strategy
notes:
C. Dyer discussed the Industrial Land Readiness Interim Funding Strategy report, noting that it was a response to a previous Committee meeting's request for staff to present an interim plan. He emphasized the absence of shovel-ready industrial parcels in the Region and outlined the recommendations put forth. Rod Regier, Commissioner of Planning, Development & Legislative Services, highlighted the ongoing challenge of a chronic shortage of shovel-ready land for investment, anticipating continued pressure in that marketplace.

In response to a question from the Committee, C. Dyer stated that the latest quarterly financial report suggests an anticipated modest surplus at the end of the year, estimated to be in the range of $3 million.

Members of the Committee engaged in a discussion regarding the Region of Waterloo International Airport, the financial implications of the proposed recommendations, and the prioritization of industrial land acquisition and servicing for the current budget year.

items.title: Councillor C. James
notes:
Councillor C. James addressed her motion, discussing the challenges associated with addressing systemic justice issues concerning youth, health, and collaborating with community organizations focused on addressing disparities.

In response to a question from the Committee, Connie MacDonald, Chief Communications & Strategy Officer, provided insight into the Community Capacity Building fund. She explained that it was established as part of the council-approved equity fund, representing a one-time allocation within the upstream fund process. As staff actively work on equity initiatives in the Region, the fund was created to support capacity building in community organizations. The opportunity was extended to the community to apply for this funding, with some organizations receiving both upstream and community capacity building funding. C. MacDonald clarified that upstream funding primarily focused on program and service delivery, while capacity building funding aimed to assist organizations in enhancing their capabilities to deliver services.

Regional Chair K. Redman proposed an amendment to the original motion, suggesting an inclusion of $1,000,000 in the 2024 Operating Budget.

items.title: Councillor C. Huinink
notes:
Councillor C. Huinink spoke to her motion, expressing that her intent was to alleviate additional strain on individuals within the community. She articulated her hope that, in the coming year, the motion would lead to further reductions in barriers to transit.

Members of the Committee discussed cash payments, accessible transit, and youth fares.

motions.text: Deferral from Community and Health Services Committee: Fee For Service Requests in the Housing Stability System CSD-HOU-23-027 That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the results of the 2023 Housing Stability System Fee for Service Request and Proposal Response Protocol (the Protocol) for the 2024 budget process as outlined in report CSD-HOU-23-027 dated November 7, 2023: a) Approve the nine service and program proposals recommended for funding in 2024 as set out Appendix A in the total amount of $3,113,493; b) Direct staff to include $3,113,493 in the 2024 Housing Services Operating Budget to fund the operating and costs of the recommended service and program proposals, with funding from the 2024 property tax levy; c) Authorize the Commissioner of Community Services and Director of Housing Services to execute any agreements, memorandums of understanding and other documents needed to implement the recommended service and program proposals, to the satisfaction of the Regional Solicitor; d) Direct Housing Services staff to enter into discussions with Marillac Residence to support a potential development of 15 units of transitional housing and 15 units of supportive housing for pregnant woman and young mothers and bring forward any recommendation to Regional Council for consideration; e) Direct Housing Services staff to enter into discussions with YWCA Cambridge to support a potential development of 20-bed 24/7 women’s emergency shelter in Cambridge and bring forward any recommendation to Regional Council for consideration; f) Direct Housing Services staff to update the Housing Stability Fee for Service Request and Proposal Protocol to further align with principles of Reconciliation, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion; and the forthcoming Plan to End Chronic Homelessness.
motions.text_html:
Deferral from Community and Health Services Committee:
Fee For Service Requests in the Housing Stability System CSD-HOU-23-027

That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the results of the 2023 Housing Stability System Fee for Service Request and Proposal Response Protocol (the Protocol) for the 2024 budget process as outlined in report CSD-HOU-23-027 dated November 7, 2023:

a) Approve the nine service and program proposals recommended for funding in 2024 as set out Appendix A in the total amount of $3,113,493;

b) Direct staff to include $3,113,493 in the 2024 Housing Services Operating Budget to fund the operating and costs of the recommended service and program proposals, with funding from the 2024 property tax levy;

c) Authorize the Commissioner of Community Services and Director of Housing Services to execute any agreements, memorandums of understanding and other documents needed to implement the recommended service and program proposals, to the satisfaction of the Regional Solicitor;

d) Direct Housing Services staff to enter into discussions with Marillac Residence to support a potential development of 15 units of transitional housing and 15 units of supportive housing for pregnant woman and young mothers and bring forward any recommendation to Regional Council for consideration;

e) Direct Housing Services staff to enter into discussions with YWCA Cambridge to support a potential development of 20-bed 24/7 women’s emergency shelter in Cambridge and bring forward any recommendation to Regional Council for consideration;

f) Direct Housing Services staff to update the Housing Stability Fee for Service Request and Proposal Protocol to further align with principles of Reconciliation, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion; and the forthcoming Plan to End Chronic Homelessness.

motions.text: Referral from Community and Health Services Committee Plan to End Chronic Homelessness CSD-HOU-23-028 That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to beginning the implementation of the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness for Regional Residents Experiencing Chronic Homelessness as set out in report CSD-HOU-23-028 dated November 7, 2023: Direct staff to begin the co-implementation of initiatives designed to address gaps identified in the Key Findings Report (CSD-HOU-23-024) with community partners, as detailed in Appendix A; Direct staff to: a) Increase the 2024 Housing Services Operating Budget by $11,124,967 to implement the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness (The Plan) funded by $3,200,000 from the Tax Stabilization Reserve and $7,924,967 from the 2024 property tax levy; b) Amend the 2024-2033 Housing capital program for the development of a hybrid shelter as outlined in this report; c) Establish a Homelessness Prevention Capital Reserve; Advocate to the Government of Canada and to the Government of Ontario for annually incremental, sustainable, and predictable funding to support both new and existing services and programs that end, prevent, and respond to experiences of homelessness; Direct staff to work with community to develop accountability and impact frameworks for the Housing Stability System; Direct staff to work with community to develop a suite of policy incentives supporting the creation of new affordable housing and/or for preventing the loss of existing affordable housing stock and tenant displacement in Waterloo Region and bring forward any further recommendations to Regional Council for consideration and approval; Authorize the Commissioner of Community Services to execute all agreements and documents required to implement resolution (a) of this report, all such agreements and documentation to be to the satisfaction of the Chief Administrator Officer, Commissioner of Community Services and the Regional Solicitor; Authorize Real Estate and Legal Services to negotiate a conditional Agreement of Purchase and Sale for property acquisition or alternative Lease Agreements that may be required for the development of initiatives under the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness, and bring forward any resulting Agreement of Purchase and Sale or Lease Agreement to Regional Council for consideration and approval, with all terms and conditions subject to the satisfaction of the Commissioner of Community Services and the Regional Solicitor.
motions.text_html:
Referral from Community and Health Services Committee Plan to End Chronic Homelessness CSD-HOU-23-028

That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to beginning the implementation of the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness for Regional Residents Experiencing Chronic Homelessness as set out in report CSD-HOU-23-028 dated November 7, 2023:

  • Direct staff to begin the co-implementation of initiatives designed to address gaps identified in the Key Findings Report (CSD-HOU-23-024) with community partners, as detailed in Appendix A;
  • Direct staff to:

a) Increase the 2024 Housing Services Operating Budget by $11,124,967 to implement the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness (The Plan) funded by $3,200,000 from the Tax Stabilization Reserve and $7,924,967 from the 2024 property tax levy;

b) Amend the 2024-2033 Housing capital program for the development of a hybrid shelter as outlined in this report;

c) Establish a Homelessness Prevention Capital Reserve;

  • Advocate to the Government of Canada and to the Government of Ontario for annually incremental, sustainable, and predictable funding to support both new and existing services and programs that end, prevent, and respond to experiences of homelessness;
  • Direct staff to work with community to develop accountability and impact frameworks for the Housing Stability System;
  • Direct staff to work with community to develop a suite of policy incentives supporting the creation of new affordable housing and/or for preventing the loss of existing affordable housing stock and tenant displacement in Waterloo Region and bring forward any further recommendations to Regional Council for consideration and approval;
  • Authorize the Commissioner of Community Services to execute all agreements and documents required to implement resolution (a) of this report, all such agreements and documentation to be to the satisfaction of the Chief Administrator Officer, Commissioner of Community Services and the Regional Solicitor;
  • Authorize Real Estate and Legal Services to negotiate a conditional Agreement of Purchase and Sale for property acquisition or alternative Lease Agreements that may be required for the development of initiatives under the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness, and bring forward any resulting Agreement of Purchase and Sale or Lease Agreement to Regional Council for consideration and approval, with all terms and conditions subject to the satisfaction of the Commissioner of Community Services and the Regional Solicitor.

motions.text: As amended: WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo is committed to advancing Truth and Reconciliation and Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion; AND WHEREAS First Nations, Inuit and Métis, African, Caribbean, Black identifying, racialized and historically under-recognized communities continue to face systemic barriers and discrimination; AND WHEREAS Organizations led by and serving these priority communities, know and understand the complex needs of their communities best, but have been traditionally under-resourced and under-funded to effectively respond; AND WHEREAS a Community Capacity Building Fund was created in response to this need and funding was distributed in 2023 alongside the Upstream Fund using budget capacity available in the Equity Fund; AND WHEREAS the Equity Fund is fully committed for a range of programs in 2024; AND WHEREAS the distribution of funding in 2023 has resulted in increased capacity for organizations led by priority-communities to support achievement of the Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan’s goals; NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED: THAT the Regional Municipality of Waterloo direct staff to include in the 2024 Operating Budget a provision of $1,000,000 to establish an annual Community Capacity Building Fund with funding from the property tax levy, and THAT staff report back in Q1 2024 with the proposed terms of reference for the Community Capacity Building Fund, incorporating the learnings from the Upstream Fund evaluation, and a timeline for application and award.
motions.text_html:
As amended:

WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo is committed to advancing Truth and Reconciliation and Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion;

AND WHEREAS First Nations, Inuit and Métis, African, Caribbean, Black identifying, racialized and historically under-recognized communities continue to face systemic barriers and discrimination;

AND WHEREAS Organizations led by and serving these priority communities, know and understand the complex needs of their communities best, but have been traditionally under-resourced and under-funded to effectively respond;

AND WHEREAS a Community Capacity Building Fund was created in response to this need and funding was distributed in 2023 alongside the Upstream Fund using budget capacity available in the Equity Fund;

AND WHEREAS the Equity Fund is fully committed for a range of programs in 2024;

AND WHEREAS the distribution of funding in 2023 has resulted in increased capacity for organizations led by priority-communities to support achievement of the Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan’s goals;

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED:

THAT the Regional Municipality of Waterloo direct staff to include in the 2024 Operating Budget a provision of $1,000,000 to establish an annual Community Capacity Building Fund with funding from the property tax levy, and

THAT staff report back in Q1 2024 with the proposed terms of reference for the Community Capacity Building Fund, incorporating the learnings from the Upstream Fund evaluation, and a timeline for application and award.

motions.text: To amend the motion so that $1,000,000 is included in the 2024 Operating Budget
motions.text_html: To amend the motion so that $1,000,000 is included in the 2024 Operating Budget

motions.text: WHEREAS an increase of the adult Grand River Transit monthly pass from the proposed $96 to $99 per month would generate as much revenue as the proposed cash fare increase from $3.75 to $4; and WHEREAS a corresponding increase of the discount rate to 52% for the Affordable Transit Program monthly pass would maintain its cost under $48 per month; and WHEREAS an increase of the Grand River Transit monthly pass to $99 per month amounts to less than the cost of one fare per day; and WHEREAS an increase of the Grand River Transit monthly pass to $99 per month is more in line with the cost of a bus pass in similar municipalities; and WHEREAS maintaining the Grand River Transit cash fare at $3.75 for the duration of 2024 will avoid putting greater financial strain on those who pay transit by cash; and THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Grand River Transit cash fares be maintained at $3.75 for the duration of 2024 and that the Grand River Transit monthly pass cost be further increased to $99 effective July 1, 2024; and THAT the discount level on the monthly pass for customers eligible to the Affordable Transit Program be increased to 52%; and THAT the 2024 User Fee and Charge By-law be prepared accordingly.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS an increase of the adult Grand River Transit monthly pass from the proposed $96 to $99 per month would generate as much revenue as the proposed cash fare increase from $3.75 to $4; and

WHEREAS a corresponding increase of the discount rate to 52% for the Affordable Transit Program monthly pass would maintain its cost under $48 per month; and

WHEREAS an increase of the Grand River Transit monthly pass to $99 per month amounts to less than the cost of one fare per day; and

WHEREAS an increase of the Grand River Transit monthly pass to $99 per month is more in line with the cost of a bus pass in similar municipalities; and

WHEREAS maintaining the Grand River Transit cash fare at $3.75 for the duration of 2024 will avoid putting greater financial strain on those who pay transit by cash; and

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Grand River Transit cash fares be maintained at $3.75 for the duration of 2024 and that the Grand River Transit monthly pass cost be further increased to $99 effective July 1, 2024; and

THAT the discount level on the monthly pass for customers eligible to the Affordable Transit Program be increased to 52%; and

THAT the 2024 User Fee and Charge By-law be prepared accordingly.
